reason: The measured 2.0 s glide prerequisite is entry_speed >= .10 + 2*|deceleration|. At the previously assumed constant ~.17 m/s^2 decay that needs .44 m/s, above the frozen public expert's measured .38 m/s plateau, so the full-stage gate looked out of reach; but the measured decay over the first .25 s of a credible glide is only -.039 m/s^2 (median +.016 over a .2 s window), and the reference four-wheel rolling decay is -.058. The loss after .25 s is therefore balance drift, not rolling resistance: lateral capture error grows .0072 -> .0203 m while the fore/aft error drifts -.015 -> +.015 m, the support-line yaw stays at .03-.18 rad (no inward support-skate steering), and every long glide ends by falling sideways, not by reaching the .10 m/s floor.
change: v16 keeps the v15 structure (task + shaping + failure) and adds: (B) a one-shot 'handoff' term paying 1.0*clamp((entry_speed-.38)/.15,0,1) once per episode, only after .25 s of credible glide, so it is exactly zero for every behaviour at or below today's ceiling and always below failure_cost; (E) a balance DEBT charged only during loaded left-only support, (|lateral|-0.008)/0.025 squared plus (|fore/aft|-0.005)/0.020 squared, accumulated into the existing smooth_debt so it discounts later glide credit instead of becoming a negative continuing reward; and (E') the same fore/aft axis added to the terminal-zero potential. Measured effect of the deadbands: 0.00 debt over 2 s at the measured p50 balance, 0.21 at p75, 2.03 at p90, 12.6 at p99. The legacy region of mdp.py (first 351782 bytes) stays byte-identical. bridge_recovery.py is added to COMPATIBLE_SOURCES so the continuation policy is pinned to the source run too, and its transition kinds are now named explicitly (actor_forward_transition / reward_forward_transition) so a record cannot silently mix them.
